observed: Opened http://localhost:4180/ on a fresh background browser tab and ran the four combinations (1440x900 light, 1440x900 dark, mobile 375x812 light, mobile 375x812 dark), each with the same in-page script. FONT SIZE: held in all four. 185 text elements scanned, smallest visible computed font-size 13.5px (code), nothing below 13px, no small ::before/::after text. CONTRAST: held in all four, for body text, a link and the selected tab (WCAG relative luminance). Light: body #1b1b18 on #fbfaf7 = 16.54, link #b4441c = 5.32, selected tab 'Git clone' #1b1b18 on its own #f2f0ea tab background = 15.15 (16.54 against the page background). Dark: body #ecebe6 on #141413 = 15.44, link #f08a5d = 7.46, selected tab on #1d1d1b = 14.14 (15.44 against the page background). No visible text anywhere on the page fell under 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text). SCREENSHOTS: four saved, same content (heading, intro, install tabs), text legible in each. HORIZONTAL SCROLL: held at 1440 (scrollWidth 1440 = innerWidth 1440 = clientWidth 1440, light and dark) but NOT at 375. In the mobile emulation the literal numbers read scrollWidth 910 and innerWidth 910 (equal), but that is an artifact: the emulator widens innerWidth to the overflowing content, while documentElement.clientWidth, visualViewport.width and outerWidth are all 375. The page is really 910px wide on a 375px screen (535px overflow). The mobile screenshots show the install command line running out of its bordered box and off the right edge. Cause: the pre inside div.command is the only element not clipped by an ancestor; div.command keeps align-items:flex-start when it switches to a column at the mobile breakpoint, so the pre takes its full line width and its own overflow-x:auto never engages (nav, tab bar and tables are overflow:auto and scroll inside their own boxes, those are fine). A second check in a plain 375px-wide viewport (hidden same-origin iframe, no mobile emulation) gave clientWidth 375, scrollWidth 473, and window.scrollTo(400,0) moved scrollX to 98.5, so the page genuinely scrolls sideways. BUILD CHANGED MID-RUN: the Vite dev server hot-updated src/App.jsx, src/styles.css and src/slices.js at 11:37 (not by me). I measured all four combinations on the earlier build (A), then re-ran all four on the newer build (B, default tab is now 'Any agent', new link in the lede). On B: desktop identical (no overflow, min font 13.5px, all contrast ratios the same); mobile still overflows, now 473 vs 375 (98px), same pre in div.command. Both builds fail the no-horizontal-scroll expectation at 375.
expected: scrollWidth equals innerWidth at every combination (no horizontal page scroll); no element with visible text has a computed font-size below 13px; body text, links and the selected tab text each reach 4.5:1 against the page background in light and dark; the four screenshots show the same content with legible text.
notes: 1) The literal check scrollWidth === innerWidth passes at 375 (910 = 910 on build A, 473 = 473 on build B) but is misleading: mobile emulation inflates innerWidth to the overflowing content width. Compare against documentElement.clientWidth / visualViewport.width (375) to see the real overflow. A script that only compares scrollWidth with innerWidth would call this a pass. 2) The dev server (Vite) was edited under me at 11:37; results for build A and build B are both saved and both fail the same way. 3) Another agent navigated my first tab (tab-5) to ?agent= mid-run (an XSS probe, apparently a parallel scenario), so I threw away that tab's mobile reading and redid everything on tab-6, addressed by id. I reset tab-5 and tab-6 to desktop at the end. 4) Browser-tool screenshots show the viewport only (800x500 for 1440x900, 750x1624 for mobile), so the mobile shots cover the top of the page; the first 1440 light screenshot came back cropped and was retaken. 5) Selected tab was 'Git clone' on build A and 'Any agent' on build B; its contrast is the same in both. 6) Nav bar, install tab bar and tables scroll inside their own overflow:auto boxes on mobile (visible scrollbar tracks, 'Models' and 'Codex plugin' are clipped until scrolled); this is contained and is not counted as page overflow. 7) The 1440 and mobile pages loaded no console errors and no failed requests.
